title: Topology optimisation solver: five acceptance checks
summary: Before a topology-optimisation code may design a chair, it has to get five simpler things right: the deflection of a clamped beam (in 2D and 3D), the rigid-body modes of its 3D element, the gradient it uses to move material, the answer of its fast multigrid solver, and the four published MBB-beam designs of Andreassen et al. (2011). This notebook runs all five with the solver of the phyein-topopt repository and compares every number with beam theory, automatic differentiation, a direct solver and the paper.
physics_sources: skills/topology-optimisation/SKILL.md, sections 2.1-2.11 (phyein-topopt at the commit above)
verification_text: Three comparisons. **Against theory and the paper**: each check has the pass limit the repository's own acceptance checks use (MBB within $10^{-4}$ of the paper, cantilever within 1 % of Timoshenko at the finest mesh, 6 rigid-body modes, gradient within $10^{-10}$ of automatic differentiation, multigrid within $10^{-6}$ of the direct solve). **Against the numbers the repository records** in `README.md` and `HANDOVER.md`, at the precision they are printed. **Against a reference run of this same notebook** made on 12 November 2026 in a Claude Code session (4 CPU cores, Python 3.13, the pinned package versions), stored in `kaggle/projects/topopt-benchmarks/reference.json`: the largest relative difference over every deterministic number is printed. A difference above the limit is a bug to find, not a number to explain away.
